footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $49.7M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 11.2% to $2.7B in 2025. Net interest income rose 13.3% to $2.2B and noninterest income rose 2.8% to $502M; noninterest expense rose 7.8%, and the provision for credit losses was $95.6M, versus $101M.
Net income to common rose 16.1% to $774M, or $11.40 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 55.5% versus 57.2%. Wintrust returned $169M through dividends.
highlights: Net income to common rose 16.1% to $774M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: Wintrust Financial Corporation Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
